subject: Transportation Systems
title: How Jet Engines Work
description: A fast breakdown of How Jet Engines Work for builders.

hook.text: A jet engine does one thing: suck air in, squeeze it, burn fuel in it, and blast it out the back.

buildup.text: Compressor blades squeeze incoming air to 30 times atmospheric pressure.

discovery.text: Fuel sprays into this compressed air and ignites. The hot gas expands violently backward.

twist.text: Newton's third law: push gas backward, the engine pushes the plane forward. Simple physics, massive power.

climax.text: A single engine on a 777 produces 115,000 pounds of thrust—enough to tow a cruise ship.

punchline.text: Suck, squeeze, bang, blow—just like a car, but faster.

quiz.question: What principle makes a jet engine produce thrust?
